svg.text: Strangler-fig refactor of the 11,625-line SipSession god object. The contract (CallCommand) is fixed; the implementation moves to small, composable structs.
proxy_call.rs routes each call: if session_engine && supports_flow(flow) → new engine, else → god object. Both live; no behaviour lost.
LEGACY — the god object & its satellites
11,625-line god object: signaling + media + DTMF + transfer + supervisor + conference + queue + CDR…
125 grep hits: SDP/ICE/codec glue scattered through the god object
String identifiers · timers/polling · shared Arc state · media+control+signaling all entangled in one type.
Destination of the refactor: this whole column is deleted once supports_flow reaches parity.

g.text: • One type owns everything → untestable, every change is high-blast-radius.
• Two media mixers (BridgePeer + ConferenceAudioMixer) + two IVR runtimes (graph + app runtime).
• WebRTC complexity inlined as “essential” when rustrtc already owns ICE/DTLS/SRTP.
• CallCommand executed inside the monolith — can’t reach a call without the god object.
BridgePeer + ConferenceAudioMixer + RtpPump → UnifiedMixer + MixerBridge + RtpSocketTask
queue_graph + app runtime + ivr/executor → CallGraph + GraphCall(CallActions) + FlowReducer + DialCall
inline WebRTC glue → WebRtcMediaBridge / WebRtcSession (rustrtc adapter)
CallCommand bus inside monolith → CommandRegistry + command_route + dispatch()
god-object leg fields → Session trait + CallSwitch + LegMap

svg.text: NEW ENGINE — built & proven (behind the flag)
builds the engine, registers the call’s command sink, pumps the SIP dialog
MEDIA PLANE — one engine: passthrough · transcode · mix · record · gain/mute · whisper
rustrtc track ⇄ RtpStreamIo (same seam as SIP)
② INTENDED — god object deleted, one engine
supports_flow widened to parity → flag default-on → A/B → delete SipSession, queue_graph, BridgePeer, ConferenceAudioMixer, RtpPump, the old runtime & the flag.
CallGraph (serde GraphDef ← visual node designer) → GraphRunner → GraphCall (CallActions)
primitives only: Play · Collect · Record · Dial · Bridge · Goto · Hangup (a menu emerges from Play→Collect→edges)
“the graph IS the switch” — no separate app runtime
returns the connected port; the bridged call outlives the walk
FlowReducer (pure, 100% testable): DialStrategy stages, failover, queue fallback → [Effect]
DialCall applies: Dial · CancelDial · AnswerCaller · Bridge · HangupCaller/Callee · End
caller hold/MoH · per-dial ring timeout · failure-audio-then-hangup
future: folded into the one CallGraph (Targets/Queue as node subgraphs)
the N-party switch. Owns legs as Box<dyn Session>
no telephony verbs in the generic trait; protocol ops are mailbox
commands returning Unsupported. take_media_io() = the media seam.
serves commands AND CDR / leg events / registry.
take_media_io() → RtpStreamIo (SIP or WebRTC — same seam)
UNIFIED MEDIA PLANE — one engine for 2-party & N-party; the tap decides per pull
Player: paces PCM as 20 ms frames

g.text: ✗ the connect_media path ✗ session_engine feature flag
CallCommand the enum stays — only its monolithic execution dies.
• Two layers: Session (durable) vs ConnectedPort (ephemeral, switch-local).
• Enums, never string ids (strings only at the wire↔enum boundary).
• Event-driven, no polling — except a real media clock for N-source mixing.
• Packet-based FIFO so passthrough is byte-exact; mixing aligns by sample count.
• The graph IS the switch — IVR/voicemail/queue are node subgraphs.
• SIP-first; generic abstraction is the fallout of clean SIP boundaries.
• GraphDef is serde config → drives a future visual node designer.
